title: What The Piano Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 104bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal music philosophy absurdist Zimbabwe Perth
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The piano has eighty-eight keys and that should be enough
But Beethoven thought otherwise and made things very rough
He wrote for a piano that hadn't been invented yet
Which is either genius or a scheduling problem — I haven't decided yet

[Pre-Chorus]
I learned to play piano for three years in my adolescence
The piano tolerated it with what I'd call professional acceptance

[Chorus]
What does the piano know that I don't know?
It knows that eighty-eight positions cover everything we feel below
What does the piano know when nobody's playing it?
It knows the next note before the hand has even started it
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The piano's been in bars and churches and front parlours
In concert halls with crystal and in basements with some hollars
Every version of the human condition has required it
And every time the piano's been there — it's never tired

[Bridge]
My father had a piano in the house in Zimbabwe
That nobody played well enough to justify the day
But it sat there in the living room as proof that something greater
Was possible — if someone practiced harder — maybe later

[Outro]
Piano knows… eighty-eight keys, the whole human condition… piano knows
That's my boy
